heard: A massive city of galaxies was flying apart too fast. Over a thousand galaxies sit 321 million light years away. Swiss astronomer Fritz Zwicky calculated their wild speeds. Visible starlight was far too weak to hold them. He realized an invisible substance must glue the cluster. That hidden dark matter outweighs all visible stars combined. Yet astronomers ignored his shocking math for 50 years. No visible force explains why those stellar systems stayed bound.
